articles.title: The Best Diner Breakfast In Every Major US Region
articles.summary: Looking for a cozy diner serving hearty fare? These are some of the best spots in the country, where you'll find all of your breakfast favorites.
articles.body:
An American diner is a casual establishment often featuring counter seating and a no-frills, nostalgic vibe. It typically offers friendly service, specials on rotation, and rather affordable comfort foods and drinks, from club sandwiches to hamburgers, pancakes, pies, coffee, and milkshakes. According to NJ Spotlight News , New Jersey is the state with the largest number of diners in the country — 530, per a 2023 count. While quantity certainly means more options, we're only concerned about quality in this article, especially in the morning hours. So, let's round up some of the most celebrated diners with outstanding breakfast offerings across the seven U.S. regions: the Mid-Atlantic, the Midwest, New England, the Pacific Coast, the Southeast, the Southwest, and the Rocky Mountains. We've selected these exceptional destinations based on criteria like accolades won, menu variety, and signature items. You can read more about our methodology at the end of the article.

Several factors should be considered when choosing a breakfast spot, even one as laid-back as a diner. Is the staff welcoming and the interior clean? Are the booths, tables, and counter seats comfortable? Are most of the ingredients fresh, and does the house offer scratch-made specialties? Is the coffee freshly brewed? Are certain dietary preferences accommodated, and can some dishes be customized? Better yet, are these portions generous enough to fuel your day? From Keyport to Chicago, Santa Fe, and Salt Lake City, the following diners easily meet the above-mentioned criteria and then some.

Mid-Atlantic: Broad Street Diner in Keyport, NJ

This train car diner was established in 1964 and has racked up many accolades. It was named Best Diner in the state by NJ.com in 2015, as well as one of the Best Diners in America for Comfort-Food Favorites by Time Out in 2026. It also won Best Casual Restaurant at the Garden State Culinary Arts Awards in 2017 and was voted Best Diner in the state by New Jersey Monthly readers in 2018. So let's take a look at what makes the convivial Broad Street Diner so special.

Customers rave about the old-school vibe, welcoming staff, prompt service, and fair prices. Plus, the portions are massive enough to share, and you can create your own omelet and breakfast sandwich. There are so many tempting options to choose from, including the aptly named Belly Buster, which consists of French toast, pancakes, or waffles with any style of eggs and your choice of bacon, sausage, pork roll, or ham. Lighter options like avocado toast and the Greek yogurt and honey bowl are also available, unless you prefer comforting specials like the fried pork steak with eggs or the pastrami sandwich.

Located on Route 66 near Union Station, the perpetually busy Lou Mitchell's has been serving outstanding house-made breakfast, brunch, and lunch since 1923. It has hosted numerous entertainment stars, professional athletes, and politicians over the decades and was added to the National Register of Historical Places in 2006. Plus, this convivial spot has earned features by the Michelin Guide and the Chicago Sun-Times.

Lou Mitchell's prides itself on its long tradition of welcoming ladies and children with free Milk Duds and offering all customers complimentary donut holes. Plus, the house-made marmalade is out of this world, and the light-roast coffee blend has won several Golden Cup awards. At this historic breakfast spot, the orange and grapefruit juices are always freshly squeezed, the locally sourced bacon is of premium quality, and the pancakes and waffles are made with local eggs and whipped butter. Those tantalizing bakery specials are all prepared daily, while fries are always hand-cut and cooked in premium peanut oil. With all these perks in mind, be sure to leave some room for Lou Mitchell's famous jumbo omelets, which feature fresh sour cream, cottage cheese, and mushrooms. The menu also includes gluten-free options.

New England: Red Arrow Diner in New Hampshire

Known for its attentive service, hospitable vibe, and flavorful offerings, Red Arrow is a must-visit 24-hour diner that was founded in 1922. With locations in Manchester, Concord, Londonderry, and Nashua, this establishment has welcomed many public figures, including congressional and presidential candidates. Not only was it featured on "Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives," but it also won Best Breakfast and Best of the Best Late Night Eats at The Hippo Best of 2026 Awards. The house offers an all-day breakfast, lunch, and dinner menu in addition to specialty dishes like fried French toast and pork pie with eggs.

Fun fact: Each Red Arrow Diner location serves about 500,000 breakfasts a year, and the choices can be overwhelming. Just consider the various cheesy hash brown specials, which feature grilled onions mixed with options like chili, chicken-fried steak (arguably the most Texan food there is) , or ham and are served with two eggs and toast. Toast options include sourdough, rye, raisin, and gluten-free.

Pacific Coast: Beth's Café in Seattle, WA

Seattle isn't just known for its upscale, hard-to-access restaurants . It's also home to unassuming eateries such as Beth's Café, whose walls are covered in works of art from visitors. Established in 1954 by Beth and Harold Eisenstadt (hence the name), this diner is located minutes from downtown Seattle and currently operates 24/7. It has been featured on the Travel Channel's "Man vs. Food" and "World's Best Places to Pig Out" as well as Food Network's "Top 5 Big Breakfasts." Plus, this spot was voted Best Place to Cure a Hangover by Seattle Magazine.

Beth's is celebrated for its huge portions, including the famous six- and 12-egg omelets . Even if you order a simple three-egg scramble, you'll still be able to enjoy all-you-can-eat hash browns. Alternatively, you can opt for crowd-pleasers like the breakfast burrito or the buttermilk biscuits with gravy. Don't forget to pair your meal with a nostalgic float and top it with treats like the enormous cinnamon rolls.

Southeast: The Silver Skillet Restaurant in Atlanta, GA

Founded in 1967, The Silver Skillet is renowned for classic Southern foods like skillet country ham, elevated with red-eye gravy, as well as staples from the state of Georgia . This famous family breakfast spot has welcomed many celebrities over the years, including Luke Perry, John O'Hurley, and Dave Chapelle. You have probably spotted it in productions like "Taken 3," Netflix's "Ozark," "Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives," and PBA's "Atlanta's Hidden Treasures." You may have even read about it in The New York Times, USA Today, and The Atlanta Business Chronicle, among many other trusted publications. In short, The Silver Skillet is beloved by amateur foodies, critics, and industry professionals alike.

All breakfast plates and omelets are served with grits or gravy and toast or biscuits. Biscuit specialties include applewood-smoked bacon, egg and cheese, and smoked link sausage, so you're in for some remarkably fluffy, melt-in-your-mouth goodness. The house's signature dessert is a lemon icebox pie, a nostalgic treat you probably ate growing up in the South . This dessert alone is worth the detour.

The Pantry, established in 1948, offers delicious breakfast options all day long. This family-owned diner serves scratch-made American and New Mexican favorites prepared from the freshest ingredients. You can feel the enthusiasm and dedication in every bite, not to mention the substantial servings and attentive, warm service. It's no wonder this cozy, community-oriented eatery won first place for Best Breakfast in the Santa Fe Reporter's Best of Santa Fe 2025 awards.

The breakfast selection is split into five sections: traditional, New Mexican, off the griddle, omelets, and two-egg specialties. According to the menu, the produce is fresh and seasonal, the cinnamon rolls are baked in house, and the corned beef is a must-try specialty. In short, those options cater to various preferences, be it a classic granola bowl, huevos rancheros, chilaquiles, or a veggie omelet. You'll find it hard to resist the decadent, cornflake-crusted French toast, which comes stuffed with cream cheese, strawberries, and blueberries and topped with a berry compote.

The Rocky Mountains: Ruth's Diner in Salt Lake City, UT

Ruth's Diner, housed in a trolley car located inside Emigration Canyon, just minutes from downtown Salt Lake City, boasts stunning mountain views. It was launched as Ruth's Hamburgers in 1930 and is therefore considered Utah's second-longest operating restaurant (after the Idle Isle Café in Brigham City). Named Best Diner for Breakfast as well as Most Famous Restaurant in The Beehive State, this spot has received multiple State of the Plate nods from Gastronomic Salt Lake City. Plus, it has been spotlighted by Utah Stories, "Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives," and Only in Utah.

All menu favorites are served with your choice of hash browns, Spanish rice with pinto beans, or cottage cheese. They include pulled pork eggs Benedict, huevos rancheros, and a potato burrito. However, it's the particularly light and fluffy Mile High biscuits, served with country-style gravy and raspberry jam, are worth the trip and wait time, as per City Cast Salt Lake and numerous visitors. The latter are equally partial to the cinnamon roll French toast with orange cream cheese. You'll also find various gluten-free and vegan options to savor for breakfast.

4160 Emigration Canyon Rd, Salt Lake City, UT 84108

To curate this list of greatest diners for breakfast across the main U.S. regions, we started by picking long-standing, widely acclaimed establishments known for their welcoming, attentive service, good value, and hearty breakfast options. Next, we looked at their signature, scratch-made dishes, desserts, and beverages, as well as their commitment to fresh and premium ingredients. Finally, glowing customer feedback on platforms like Google Reviews, Reddit, Yelp, and Tripadvisor, in addition to features by media outlets and regional guides, was taken into consideration.

articles.title: A demand to vacate house, trip to Delhi & murder in 15 minutes: How couple killed DU professor
articles.summary: Delhi Police chargesheet says Bardhaman tenants killed DU professor Debosmita Paul in 15 minutes after eviction demand; couple used fake IDs, CCTV traced.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A demand to vacate an ancestral property in West Bengal’s Bardhaman allegedly led a couple to hatch a plan to murder Delhi University professor Debosmita Paul at her residence in east Delhi’s Vasundhara Enclave in June, police have stated in their chargesheet.The couple allegedly took about 15 minutes to enter the society, kill Paul, change clothes and leave. The change of clothes, however, gave them away. Their young son, who was present at the spot, has been made a witness in the case.The chargesheet, filed in the first week of Sept, contains statements from more than 40 witnesses and runs into over 300 pages. The couple were booked for murder, criminal conspiracy, impersonation and other offences.Paul and her mother jointly owned an ancestral property spread over more than 1,000 square yards in Bardhaman. The accused couple had been living as tenants on the ground floor, with the rent deposited into Paul’s and her mother’s joint bank account. Paul had visited the property with her mother last year and told the couple they would have to vacate it. She initially asked them to leave by June and reiterated the demand on the phone in March this year.Police alleged that the husband, who works at a hardware shop, discussed the issue with his wife and they decided to kill Paul so they could continue living on the property. They allegedly believed other members of Paul’s family had little interest in the property and that they could eventually take control of it.The husband allegedly travelled to Delhi three times before the murder for a recce, observing Paul’s routine, residence and educational activities, the chargesheet states. On June 2, the couple travelled from Bardhaman to Delhi along with their son, aged 10, checked into a hotel, and allegedly carried out the murder the following day. They rang Paul’s doorbell, knowing she was familiar with them, and told her they had come to discuss the Bardhaman property. Once inside, they handed their young son a phone and went into another room.The accused allegedly attacked Paul on the head with a mortar before repeatedly striking her face and slitting both her wrists. Their son heard the commotion and entered the room, where he witnessed the incident, police said.Investigators said the entire sequence -- from the point the accused entered the society till they carried out the murder, changed clothes and then left -- took about 15 minutes. To evade detection, the duo allegedly changed their clothes at Paul’s house. They also used fake Aadhaar cards during their stay at the hotel.Police analysed footage from more than 500 CCTV cameras during the investigation. Footage from Paul’s society showed a masked couple entering around 3.20pm with a child and later leaving, with the two adults having changed clothes and the child still wearing the same clothes.Investigators questioned the cab driver who had dropped the family near Dallupura and traced their movements to the hotel where they had stayed. Hotel records showed the man was from Bihar and the woman from Bardhaman, prompting police to examine their links to the property.The couple was later traced to Anand Vihar. Instead of taking a train from there, they travelled to New Delhi railway station before boarding a train for Bardhaman. A police team reached Bardhaman, where investigators traced a scooter allegedly used by the accused, conducted door-to-door searches at more than 100 houses, and finally arrested the couple. articles.title: Watch: RTC bus swerves to avoid wrong-way car, ploughs into petrol bunk
articles.summary: RTC bus crashed into a petrol bunk at Batasingaram after swerving to avoid a wrong-way car; no injuries, two cars and an installation damaged, probe on.
articles.body: HYDERABAD: A bus driver’s attempt to avoid a car that allegedly entered a service road from the wrong direction resulted in an RTC bus crashing into a petrol bunk at Batasingaram in Abdullapurmet.No injuries were reported in the incident, a video of which has since gone viral on social media.According to Abdullapurmet police, a case was registered against the RTC bus driver based on a complaint lodged by the petrol bunk manager, alleging damage to two cars and a fixed installation on the premises.Police said two cars were waiting to refuel when the bus, travelling along the service road, suddenly veered into the petrol bunk and collided with the vehicles and an installation. Bunk employees ran to safety after noticing the bus approaching at high speed. The bus eventually came to a halt inside the premises.However, an examination of CCTV footage revealed that a parked truck on the service road and a car that allegedly entered from the wrong direction contributed to the incident. Police said the bus driver’s view was obstructed by the parked truck, and he swerved left to avoid colliding with the car that suddenly appeared in front of him.Despite the evasive manoeuvre, the bus entered the petrol bunk and damaged two cars before coming to a stop. articles.title: Now, SIR confusion over Karnataka CM DK Shivakumar’s mom, Zerodha’s Kamaths
articles.summary: Special Intensive Revision of Karnataka voter rolls flags name mismatches for CM DK Shivakumar’s mother, Nandan Nilekani and Zerodha’s Kamaths; verification ongoing.
articles.body: BENGALURU: Instances of name mismatch in the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls continue to create waves of confusion among VIP families. Days after Bharat Ratna CNR Rao and actor Shivarajkumar figured in the verification exercise, it’s the turn of the Karnataka chief minister’s mother and Infosys co-founder Nandan Nilekani to produce documents over logical discrepancies in voter records.In none of these cases, VIPs and their family members were called to the BBMP offices.While the Nilekani family has completed verification, Zerodha’s Kamath brothers and their mother are awaiting clarity.Bengaluru South district election officers said the name of DK Shivakumar’s mother Gowramma was flagged for mismatch in Kanakapura assembly constituency. However, she was not among those served notice. “The confusion arose from names with similar spellings. Reports on the visual media are not factually correct,” an officer said.Officials said three voters named Gowramma are listed in part no. 249 of Kanakapura constituency. The CM’s mother, Gowramma w/o Kempegowda, is listed at serial no. 1 with EPIC ZVG4032298. Notices were issued to the other two voters with the same name.In the case of the Nilekanis, SIR verification was completed Thursday. Officials said notices had been generated for Nilekani and his family under the no-mapping category. Since Nilekani falls under the VIP category, the booth-level officer visited his residence to complete verification.Nilekani’s staff sought copies of the notices before submitting documents, including details of the family’s enrolment in the 2002 rolls. The BLO later delivered the notices and returned on Thursday to collect the documents and complete the process. The Nilekanis are enrolled in Koramangala under BTM Layout assembly constituency.Ramesh KN, additional district election officer, Bengaluru South, said there was confusion over reports of notices issued to Zerodha founders Nikhil and Nithin Kamath. Officials from Bengaluru South City Corporation and urban district administration contacted their mother, Revathi Kamath, who clarified that the family had not received any notices. “We are verifying whether notices were generated in their names,” he said. articles.title: US and Indian armies kick off ‘Yudh Abhyas 2026’, counter-drone systems being used for first time; Sergio Gor says 'learning from each other, building trust and capabilities
articles.summary: News News: NEW DELHI: The United States Army and Indian Army have commenced Exercise Yudh Abhyas 2026, marking the 22nd iteration of the premier annual bilateral.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The United States Army and Indian Army have commenced Exercise Yudh Abhyas 2026, marking the 22nd iteration of the premier annual bilateral training event between the two nations. This year’s exercise, which started on Wednesday, will go on till Sept 28 at two places — Bikaner in Rajasthan and Auli in Uttarakhand.This year’s training features the deployment of Arctic-trained Soldiers from the US Army’s 11th Airborne Division, based at Fort Wainwright, Alaska, to the high-altitudes of India. The exercise is bolstered by the participation of the 3rd Multi-Domain Task Force, introducing advanced long-range precision fires and integrated command-and-control systems to the bilateral framework.Operating under the strategic framework of Operation Pathways, this year’s exercise marks a historic milestone with the first-of-its-kind deployment of advanced counter-drone systems to India. The integration of the mobile low, slow, small unmanned aircraft integrated defeat system (MLIDS) allows both nations to adapt together to emerging battlefield threats and reinforce regional readiness.US ambassador to India Sergio Gor and Lieutenant General Joel “JB” Vowell, the Deputy Commanding General for US Army Pacific, are scheduled to attend key training events, underscoring the strength of the US-India defence partnership. “Yudh Abhyas shows just how strong the US-India defence partnership has become,” said Sergio Gor. “Our soldiers are training together, learning from each other, and building the trust and capabilities that make both of our countries stronger and more secure,” he said.While the ambassador highlighted the strategic ties, Vowell emphasised the operational reach and practical readiness that the annual bilateral exercise delivers to the joint force.“Yudh Abhyas is about building trust, sharing expertise, and demonstrating our commitment to a free and open Indo-Pacific,” Vowell said. “Every year, our partnership with the Indian Army grows stronger, and together we are ready to meet any challenge,” he said.This year’s exercise features a command post exercise and a field training exercise, culminating in a combined live-fire demonstration. This event will showcase the digital integration of several US and Indian long-range and precision fires and rocket systems.

articles.title: Emma Bonino, ícone do feminismo italiano, morre aos 78 anos | G1
articles.standfirst: Veterana das lutas pelo direito ao divórcio e ao aborto, Bonino foi integrante do Partido Radical italiano e fundou seu próprio depois: Mais Europa.
articles.summary: Veterana das lutas pelo direito ao divórcio e ao aborto, Bonino foi integrante do Partido Radical italiano e fundou seu próprio depois: Mais Europa.
articles.body:
Emma Bonino, política e ícone do feminismo italiano — Foto: AP Photo/Luca Bruno

A histórica ativista italiana Emma Bonino, uma das figuras políticas mais populares e respeitadas do país, morreu aos 78 anos de idade, anunciou seu partido nesta sexta-feira (11).

Veterana das lutas pelo direito ao divórcio e ao aborto, Bonino foi integrante do Partido Radical italiano e recebeu o reconhecimento em todo o espectro político.

"Hoje perdemos não apenas nossa líder, mas também uma das figuras mais lúcidas, corajosas e livres da história política do nosso país", afirmou o pequeno partido Mais Europa, fundado por ela.

Emma Bonino foi comissária europeia e ministra das Relações Exteriores da Itália , mas era conhecida sobretudo por sua militância feminista e por seu compromisso com as causas humanitárias.

A primeira-ministra da Itália , Giorgia Meloni , prestou homenagem e afirmou que, embora suas "trajetórias e visões fossem diferentes", isso nunca a impediu de reconhecer "sua importância e papel na vida pública da nossa nação".

articles.title: Chuva na região de Campinas: Sumaré tem recorde e Monte Mor alaga | G1
articles.standfirst: Sumaré registrou 101 mm em 24 horas, maior acumulado entre os pontos monitorados no estado. Em Monte Mor, Rio Capivari ficou 1,36 metro acima da cota de transbordamento.
articles.summary: Com 101 mm em 24 horas, Sumaré lidera acumulados em SP enquanto a Defesa Civil monitora quedas de muros em Campinas e o transbordamento do Rio Capivari.
articles.body:
A chuva forte que atingiu a região de Campinas entre quinta-feira (10) e a madrugada desta sexta (11) provocou alagamentos em Sumaré (SP), elevou o nível do Rio Capivari em Monte Mor (SP) e deixou estragos em Campinas (SP).

Sumaré registrou 101 mm de chuva em 24 horas no ponto de medição do Rio Quilombo, o maior acumulado entre os equipamentos monitorados pelo Centro Nacional de Monitoramento e Alertas de Desastres Naturais (Cemaden) e pelo Instituto Nacional de Meteorologia (Inmet) no estado.

Veja os principais impactos registrados na região:

Sumaré: houve alagamento na Vila Diva, perto do Ribeirão Quilombo. A cidade registrou 101 mm de chuva em 24 horas;

Monte Mor: o Rio Capivari ficou 1,36 metro acima da cota de referência de transbordamento, e o município acionou o plano de contingência;

Campinas: houve alagamentos, quedas de árvores e de muros. Um veículo ficou preso em um ponto alagado, e duas vias chegaram a ser totalmente bloqueadas por árvores de grande porte.

Valinhos : um alagamento interditou uma alça do Trevo de Valinhos, no Anel Viário Magalhães Teixeira.

Paulínia : acumulou 78 mm de chuva entre a madrugada e a manhã. Houve um registro de fiação rompida na região central, sem vítimas ou alagamentos.

Em Sumaré, equipes da Defesa Civil foram mobilizadas para acompanhar um ponto de alagamento na Vila Diva, perto do Ribeirão Quilombo.

Segundo a prefeitura, as equipes permaneceram no local monitorando a situação e avaliando as condições de segurança para os moradores.

O município também permaneceu em atenção diante da possibilidade de chuva moderada a forte e de novos alagamentos urbanos.

A Defesa Civil orientou a população a evitar áreas alagadas, não atravessar trechos com acúmulo de água e procurar locais seguros durante períodos de chuva intensa .

Além dos 101 mm registrados no Rio Quilombo, o acumulado chegou a 99 mm na Vila Miranda.

Alagamentos em Sumaré, na região da Vila Diva, na manhã desta sexta-feira (11) — Foto: Rodrigo Takamoto

Em Monte Mor, o Rio Capivari ficou 1,36 metro acima da cota de referência de transbordamento , segundo a Defesa Civil.

Moradores dos bairros Capuavinha, Progresso e Farid Calil, além do Condomínio Pontim, foram orientados sobre a situação.

Diante da elevação do rio, a prefeitura acionou o Plano de Contingência , com mobilização de secretarias municipais para monitorar áreas de risco e atender famílias que eventualmente precisassem de assistência.

Uma família chegou a acionar a Defesa Civil durante a madrugada, mas depois desistiu do atendimento. Até o início da manhã, não havia registro de pessoas desabrigadas ou desalojadas .

Nas medições feitas pelo município, o acumulado de chuva em 24 horas chegou a 73,8 mm no Jardim Paviotti, 65,2 mm nas Chácaras Mirim, 64,5 mm na Ponte Siqueira Campos, 56,6 mm no Cônego Cyriaco e 55,7 mm em Santa Cruz.

Campinas tem alagamentos, quedas de árvores e muros

Em Campinas, a chuva provocou alagamentos, quedas de árvores e de muros durante a madrugada e o início da manhã desta sexta-feira.

A Defesa Civil registrou, entre 3h14 e 5h45, uma queda de galho na Via Expressa Waldemar Paschoal, na região Leste, e duas quedas de muros no Jardim Maracanã, na região Noroeste.

Também foram registradas as seguintes ocorrências:

Avenida Heitor Penteado: alagamento de média proporção na pista interna, próximo ao Kartódromo. Não houve bloqueio, e agentes monitoravam o local;

Rua Alberto Bosco, na Nova Aparecida: queda de uma árvore de grande porte próximo à Rua Afonso Legaz Garcia. A via foi totalmente bloqueada, e a Defesa Civil foi acionada para a retirada;

Avenida da Saudade: uma árvore de grande porte caiu próximo à Avenida Ângelo Simões e bloqueou totalmente a via. O Corpo de Bombeiros realizava a poda, enquanto agentes auxiliavam na sinalização e orientação dos motoristas;

Rua Alfredo da Costa Figo: um alagamento de grande proporção, próximo à Rua Arquiteto José Augusto Silva, deixou um veículo preso na água. Um guincho foi acionado para a remoção.

Um ponto de medição no Ribeirão das Cabras acumulou 88 mm de chuva em 24 horas, enquanto outro, no Satélite Íris I, registrou 58 mm.

Em Valinhos (SP), um alagamento interditou uma alça do Trevo de Valinhos, no Anel Viário Magalhães Teixeira (SP-083), na manhã desta sexta-feira.

Segundo a Rota das Bandeiras, concessionária responsável pelo trecho, o bloqueio não provocava lentidão. Havia excesso de veículos no sentido da Rodovia D. Pedro I, movimento que, de acordo com a empresa, é comum para o horário.

articles.title: Google unveils five new sustainability initiatives in India
articles.summary: Tech News News: Google is expanding its Solar API to cover more than 300 million rooftops in India, enabling faster and more accurate rooftop solar assessments. Insta.
articles.body: Google is expanding its Solar API to cover more than 300 million rooftops in India, enabling faster and more accurate rooftop solar assessments. Installers can now evaluate a home’s solar potential without an on‑site visit, reducing time and cost. Platforms like Solar Ladder and OpenSolar have already integrated Solar API insights to streamline proposal creation and automate manual roof surveys.Google has signed a long‑term agreement with ReNew Power for a 150‑megawatt solar project in Rajasthan. The company will receive environmental attributes from the clean electricity generated, helping address electricity‑related emissions across its value chain. This marks Google’s second Scope 3‑focused solar project in India, bringing total added capacity to 300 MW.Google is partnering with Mitti Labs to help tens of thousands of smallholder rice farmers adopt Alternate Wetting and Drying (AWD), a climate‑smart farming method that reduces methane emissions and conserves water. The initiative is expected to generate up to 3 million tonnes of CO₂e in near‑term warming impact (GWP20) and conserve billions of gallons of water. NASA‑enabled satellite verification will support monitoring and farmer adoption.The Google Center for Climate Technology has selected three inaugural projects focused on green workforce training and low‑carbon construction materials. Google is adding two new focus areas—water stewardship and waste & circularity—and is inviting proposals via the Manthan Platform. Selected applicants will receive support to develop scalable, data‑driven environmental solutions.Google has welcomed the first cohort of the DeepMind Accelerator: AI for the Planet, featuring four Indian startups: Terrastack, Varaha Climate, Farmers for Forests, and Climitra Carbon. These companies use AI, Geo‑AI, drones and satellite models to empower farmers, scale agroforestry, restore biodiversity, and convert biomass into biochar.These five initiatives reflect Google’s push to combine AI, research partnerships and local innovation to advance sustainable development and climate resilience across India.Get the latest technology news and updates. articles.title: Maharashtra CM's wife Amruta Fadnavis invites Jarange home for meal, he picks Bhaubeej day
articles.summary: MUMBAI: Amruta Fadnavis is usually known to speak her mind on issues. Just a day after the CM's wife opposed religious curbs on participation in garba.
articles.body: MUMBAI: Amruta Fadnavis is usually known to speak her mind on issues. Just a day after the CM's wife opposed religious curbs on participation in garba events, she reached out to Maratha quota activist Manoj Jarange, describing him as her brother and inviting him home for a meal.Jarange, unrelenting in his criticism of Devendra Fadnavis amidst a hunger strike for Maratha quota, appeared restrained in his response. He said it was not the right time for him to visit the CM's residence. However, if the offer was intended with "affection and compassion", he would meet her during Bhaubeej, a festival after Diwali that celebrates the brother-sister bond. Jarange said he was determined to travel to Mumbai in coming days, but to press for his demands. He said he would spell out his plan on Sept 12. tnn & agenciesAmruta Fadnavis’s invitation to Jarange came as she spoke to reporters in Nagpur on Wednesday. Asked about the activist, she said, “Jarange Patilji is my brother, and I invite him for a meal at our home.”Manoj Jarange has been staging a hunger strike to demand reservation for the Maratha community under the Other Backward Classes (OBC) category. He has also been seeking issuance of Kunbi caste certificates to eligible members of the Maratha community.“If the brother is agitating, the sister should not call at this moment for food. The brother will have a problem. The sister should think about it and call me on Bhaubeej...will go with a saree (for her), and this is my word,” Jarange said on Thursday. He said if someone speaks with good intention, there is no need to question it every time.“If you are calling me from the battlefield, then I have to accept defeat. If someone is saying something with a good feeling, there is no need to take it otherwise. But this is not the time to go on her invitation because the brother is currently fighting for the kids of poor people,” he added.Asked about no govt representatives coming to meet him, Jarange said he did not wait for anyone in the past three years of his agitation. “I am agitating on my own capacity. The (govt) delegation will behave according to the way it is guided. It is okay when there is one guide. If guides from various thought schools come together, it creates a mess.”Reiterating his plan, Jarange said, “I am definitely going to Mumbai and will declare the date on Sept 12. A police source said the plumber had cautioned the accused against breaking the wall after noticing the construction work at the property.“During the investigation, we found out that one of the plumbers had warned the accused hours before the incident not to break the wall as it could lead to a collapse. However, the warning was allegedly ignored. We are verifying the testimony and other details related to the sequence of events,” the source said.Sources said the load-bearing wall was allegedly removed during construction and may have weakened the structure, contributing to its collapse.During questioning, PG operator Sudhanshu Lovneesh, 31, allegedly told investigators that he had asked Mahesh, the building owner’s son, about the construction and why it was being carried out. Police, however, have so far found nothing to corroborate his claim.Investigators are questioning neighbours and others in the area to establish whether they had noticed the construction activity or raised concerns before the collapse. They are also reconstructing the sequence of work carried out at the property and examining the roles of those involved.A senior police officer, when asked about a purported letter sent by police to the government seeking an inspection of PGs in Satya Niketan over alleged lack of fire safety measures a few months ago, said he was not aware of the specific communication. articles.summary: Tech News News: Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu has raised concerns about the growing use of frontier AI models by companies handling sensitive information. Quoting Fields.
articles.body: Zoho founder Sridhar Vembu has raised concerns about the growing use of frontier AI models by companies handling sensitive information. Quoting Fields Medalist Terence Tao, Sridhar Vembu shared an X (formerly Twitter) post that said companies with critical know-how, intellectual property and trade secrets should be careful about trusting their information with frontier AI labs. The mathematician warned that AI could change how researchers share ideas. Tao said, "The incentives may now be pointing in the direction of no longer sharing any promising research directions with the broader community, which would reverse centuries of traditions of open science and do serious long-term damage to the future of the field".Sridhar Vembu raises AI data security concernsSridhar Vembu said companies with valuable intellectual property and trade secrets should be cautious about putting their information into frontier AI systems. "This is quite serious and it is not just mathematicians and scientists," Vembu wrote.He argued that the concern could apply to companies across industries that have sensitive information they do not want to expose outside their organisations.In the post, Vembu also highlighted the pharmaceutical industry as an example. He said major pharma companies already have their own AI models, often based on open-source models, to avoid giving large AI companies information about new drug molecules and processes they are developing."That caution is well warranted," Sridhar Vembu said.Zoho founder says companies should build their own AI models"Your company's know-how belongs in your own AI model," Vembu wrote. He also said that building and running private AI models is becoming easier and cheaper. “Fortunately they are easy to train and becoming cheaper to run too”.Get the latest technology news and updates. articles.title: JD Vance defends Usha's heritage, hits out at Michigan Senate candidate El-Syed
articles.summary: US News: US Vice President JD Vance used his address at the Republican National Convention to launch a fresh attack on Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed.
articles.body: US Vice President JD Vance used his address at the Republican National Convention to launch a fresh attack on Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed over remarks about his wife, Usha Vance, before turning his ire on a protester waving a Mexican flag during the speech.Vance accused El-Sayed, a Democratic candidate for the US Senate from Michigan, of judging his late grandfather, James Vance, based on race and questioning whether he could have genuinely loved Usha, an Indian-American Hindu.“He looks at him, sees the color of his skin, and decides that he could never have loved my wife,” Vance said.The remarks came after Vance and El-Sayed had exchanged barbs over comments about Usha and Vance’s family. During an August campaign appearance in Detroit, Vance had told El-Sayed to “keep my wife’s name” out of his mouth after the Democrat suggested Vance’s late grandfather might have disapproved of his marriage.Vance then broadened his attack to the Democratic Party, accusing it of becoming “the party of hatred” and saying it had abandoned the traditions associated with former presidents Franklin D Roosevelt, John F Kennedy and Bill Clinton.The vice president also defended the Trump administration’s record on border security, tax cuts and what he described as traditional values.During the speech, Vance was speaking about what he called “birthright” American values when a protester interrupted him while holding a Mexican flag. Vance told the heckler to leave the US and offered to buy him a ticket to Mexico.“If you love Mexico so much, get your a** over there. I’ll buy you the plane ticket,” Vance said.“We got to send a message this November,” Vance said. “This country was handed down to us by our parents and their parents before them. We received this national birthright, and we are going to fight for it by electing Republicans this November.”The protester was later escorted out of the American Airlines Center as Republican supporters and delegates cheered.Vance also referred to the late conservative activist Charlie Kirk while discussing criticism of the administration’s handling of the Iran war. He said Kirk had opposed war but had also demonstrated that people could disagree politically while continuing to work towards what they believed was best for the country.“I think Charlie is a great example of how to disagree, but still participate in the work of saving this country,” the vice president said. “He did not always agree with us. Let me just give you one example: Charlie hated war.”“Of course, there are people who love what we’ve done, people who don’t. I’m not here to litigate the disagreements,” Vance added. “But what I’m asking you to do is do what Charlie did. Do not throw the baby out with your bathwater.”Vance ended his remarks on Kirk by stressing the importance of voting for Republicans, saying Americans should not hand the country over to “a bunch of crazy people” because of disagreements over policy.Vance is expected to be a potential contender for the Republican presidential nomination in 2028.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: After 9/11, Canada’s tiny town of Gander sheltered 7,000 Americans for days, providing food and refuge as 38 planes landed there following the attack
articles.summary: US News: Long before the trade tariffs, barriers and diplomatic tensions between the US and Canada, there was a time when thousands of Americans found unexpect.
articles.body: Long before the trade tariffs, barriers and diplomatic tensions between the US and Canada, there was a time when thousands of Americans found unexpected refuge in a tiny Canadian town after 9/11. On September 11, 2001, residents of a small Canadian town thousands of miles from New York suddenly found themselves caring for thousands of strangers caught up in an unprecedented crisis. When the United States closed its airspace following the terrorist attacks, 38 passenger planes crossing the Atlantic were diverted to Gander in Newfoundland and Labrador. The town, with a population of fewer than 10,000 people, suddenly had to accommodate around 7,000 passengers and crew. Schools, churches, community centres and homes became temporary shelters, while residents supplied food, clothing and other essentials. What began as an emergency quickly became an extraordinary display of hospitality, with ordinary people opening their doors to frightened travellers who had no idea when they would be able to continue their journeys.A Canadian town suddenly filled with stranded American passengersGander was uniquely positioned to receive the diverted aircraft because of its long aviation history. Located on the northeastern island of Newfoundland, the town had once been a major refuelling point for aircraft crossing the North Atlantic. Its airport was among the world's most important aviation hubs before advances in aircraft technology made longer non-stop flights possible. On September 11, however, its historic role suddenly returned in dramatic fashion. As flights were diverted from US airspace, 38 aircraft landed at Gander International Airport, bringing thousands of passengers into a community that had never expected to accommodate so many people at once.Residents opened their homes and community buildingsThe scale of the challenge was enormous. Gander and nearby communities had to find places for thousands of passengers while aircraft remained grounded and travellers waited for information. Residents responded by transforming everyday spaces into temporary shelters. Schools, churches and public buildings were opened, while people brought food, clothing, toiletries and other necessities. Some locals invited complete strangers into their homes. The response was not limited to organised emergency services. Shopkeepers, teachers, cooks, hotel workers, students and ordinary families all found ways to help people who had suddenly been separated from their normal journeys and, in many cases, from their families.The stranded passengers could not simply leave the airport and continue their journeys. They remained in the region for several days as the international aviation system dealt with the unprecedented disruption. During that period, the people of Gander and surrounding communities continued providing meals, accommodation and practical assistance. Passengers were able to contact relatives, receive medical help when needed and find basic comforts while waiting. The Canadian government's account of the episode records more than 6,500 passengers and crew being accommodated in Gander, while the widely told story of the town often rounds the figure to around 7,000 people.The response became a symbol of Canadian generosityWhat happened in Gander gradually became one of the most enduring stories of kindness to emerge from the aftermath of 9/11. There were no elaborate preparations for such an influx of people and no expectation that the town would suddenly become a refuge for thousands of international travellers. Yet residents responded with an instinctive willingness to help. Their actions became a powerful example of how a small community could respond to a crisis on an international scale. The episode also strengthened the already close relationship between Canada and the United States at a moment when Americans were experiencing shock, fear and uncertainty.The story later reached BroadwayThe extraordinary events in Gander eventually became the subject of the musical Come From Away. The production tells the story of passengers stranded in Newfoundland and the residents who cared for them. It brought the experience of Gander to audiences far beyond Canada and the United States and became an internationally recognised stage production. The musical's popularity helped turn what might otherwise have remained a remarkable local episode into a lasting part of the public memory of 9/11.Gander still remembers what happenedMore than two decades later, the events remain deeply embedded in the town's identity. Gander continues to commemorate September 11, with the anniversary serving as a reminder of the unusual connection formed between the community and the passengers who arrived there unexpectedly. The North Atlantic Aviation Museum and other local attractions also preserve the town's aviation history and its connection to the events of 2001. For many residents, however, the most important legacy is not the fame that followed but the simple principle that shaped their response at the time. People needed help, and the community helped them.The relationship with America has since changedThe warmth associated with Gander's response to 9/11 stands in sharp contrast to the strained relationship between Canada and the United States today. Under President Donald Trump, disputes over tariffs and trade have created significant tension between the two neighbouring countries. Canadian frustration has grown as Washington has pursued policies that Ottawa considers damaging to Canadian economic interests. The deterioration has been particularly striking because Canada and the United States have historically maintained one of the world's closest economic and political relationships.Canadians still distinguish Americans from their governmentDespite the political tensions, the Gander story shows that hostility towards US policies does not necessarily translate into hostility towards ordinary Americans. People in the town interviewed for the recent account continued to express a willingness to help Americans in another emergency. Some even made a clear distinction between the American people and the administration in Washington. That distinction is particularly striking because some Americans visiting Canada today reportedly feel the need to apologise for their government's actions, creating an almost complete reversal of the emotional dynamic seen after 9/11.A new generation sees America differentlyThe shift may be particularly significant among younger Canadians who have grown up with a very different image of the United States. Older Canadians often remember decades of close cultural, economic and personal connections with their southern neighbour, including frequent travel across the border and a strong influence from American television and popular culture. Younger Canadians have increasingly encountered the United States through a period of political polarisation and disputes over issues ranging from trade to reproductive rights. For them, the America remembered fondly by older generations may be more distant and less familiar.The welcome has not disappearedYet the remarkable thing about Gander is that its basic attitude towards people in need appears unchanged. The town that opened its doors to thousands of frightened passengers in 2001 remains willing to welcome visitors from the United States, provided the relationship is based on mutual respect. That gives the Gander story a meaning that goes beyond the events of one terrible day. Twenty-five years after 9/11, the town remains a reminder that international relationships are not built only by governments. Sometimes they are shaped by ordinary people who decide to help a stranger when there is no obligation to do so.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Watch: Fed up over poor  network, villagers tie technician with mobile tower
articles.summary: PRAYAGRAJ: In a bizarre incident, a group of villagers after being fed up over poor connectivity for allegedly past two years, not only made a technic.
articles.body: PRAYAGRAJ: In a bizarre incident, a group of villagers after being fed up over poor connectivity for allegedly past two years, not only made a technician of a telecom company captive but also tied him with the mobile tower for around two hours in Hardauli village of Fatehpur district on Thursday evening.After being alerted, cops posted at 112 rushed the spot and freed the technician from the clutches of villagers. On the complaint of technician, Adityabhan Singh, an FIR under section 127 (2) of BNS was lodged at Bindiki police station against unknown villagers.Basawanpur (aung) resident, Adityabhan Singh in his FIR asserted that he went to Hardauli village on Thursday evening to check power supply. In the meantime, a group of villagers arrived at the spot and involved themselves into heated arguments over poor mobile connectivity.Victim said that one of the unknown villagers suggested that others tie him with the mobile tower, then only we will get better connectivity. Following this, villagers held a mobile tower technician captive and tied him to the tower. A video of the incident has also surfaced.Cops arrived at the scene after being informed by another villager, rescued the technician from their custody, and took him to the police station.Villagers asserted that the poor connectivity was affecting phone calls, internet access and other online activities, causing inconvenience and financial losses to local residents.They also alleged that mobile users were paying high recharge charges despite receiving inadequate network service.However, sources pointed out that when villagers mounted pressure on technician to sort out their poor connectivity grievances, the tehnician himself advised the villagers to make him captive in order to take their appeal to higher ups of the telecommunication company.Villagers claimed that a private mobile company was installed in Hardauli village approximately two years back. At the time of installation, residents had hoped that the issue of poor mobile network connectivity would be resolved. However, the villagers allege that the network problem persists even after two years and there was none to listen to their grievances.A villager also recorded the video of the incident, which subsequently went viral on social media. The police learned of the matter after the video began circulating widely. Investigations are on.Stay updated with the latest Prayagraj news. Download the TOI App.

articles.title: After Trump renamed Lake Ontario 'Lake America,' a Pennsylvania Republican now wants Lake Erie renamed 'Lake Pennsylvania'
articles.summary: US News: President Donald Trump’s decision to rename Lake Ontario as “Lake America” has now been followed by a similar proposal involving another Great Lake. A.
articles.body: President Donald Trump’s decision to rename Lake Ontario as “Lake America” has now been followed by a similar proposal involving another Great Lake. A Republican lawmaker in Pennsylvania is preparing a resolution seeking to rename Lake Erie as “Lake Pennsylvania”.State Representative David Maloney argues that the state has a strong economic and cultural connection with the Great Lake. He is expected to urge President Donald Trump, Congress and Secretary of the Interior Doug Burgum to take steps towards changing the lake’s name, according to a an official statement issued by him, Newsweek reported.Maloney represents Pennsylvania’s 130th Legislative District in Berks County. He said Pennsylvanians regularly travel to Lake Erie for boating, fishing and family visits, with visitors spending money along the state’s shoreline. He also referred to research by Pennsylvania Sea Grant and said Pennsylvania stocked almost 500,000 yearling steelhead in 2025, which he said was about 40% of the steelhead stocked across the lake.The proposal comes about two weeks after Trump signed an executive order directing US federal agencies to use the name “Lake America” for Lake Ontario. Trump signed the order on August 27, during growing tensions between the United States and Canada over trade. The order requires US federal agencies to use the new name on maps, documents and databases.The Lake Ontario decision itself has faced resistance in Canada and parts of the United States. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney rejected the name change, saying the lake’s name comes from the language of the Indigenous Wendat people and predates both Canadian Confederation and the US Declaration of Independence. Several US governors in the Great Lakes region also dismissed the move.Why Maloney wants Lake Erie renamedMaloney said Pennsylvania has a particular connection with Lake Erie, which borders the state. He pointed to recreation and fishing as reasons for the proposed name change.“Ohio has plenty of shoreline. New York already has two Great Lakes. Canada has four others,” Maloney said.His office told Newsweek that the proposal is based on how Pennsylvanians care for the lake and how residents of other states also visit it for recreation and fishing. “Be proud and own it,” the office said.Lake Erie is shared by the United States and Canada. Ontario lies along its northern shore, while Michigan, Ohio, Pennsylvania and New York border it on the American side. It is the smallest Great Lake by volume and the shallowest.Where the name Lake Erie comes fromAccording to the Michigan Department of Environment, Great Lakes and Energy, the name comes from the Indigenous people who lived along its southern shore when Europeans reached the area in the early 1600s.“Erie” is a shortened form of the Iroquoian word “Erielhonan”, which means “long tail” and refers to the eastern cougar,The National Museum of the Great Lakes says Europeans discovered Lake Erie last among the Great Lakes. Control of the lake was also strategically important because it provided access to areas above Niagara Falls.Would 'Lake Pennsylvania' become official?Maloney’s proposal would face the same broader issue surrounding any US attempt to change the name of a body of water shared with another country.The US Board on Geographic Names says proposals to change existing geographic names require a compelling reason and evidence of support. The board generally discourages changes to existing names.If the federal government approved the change, “Lake Pennsylvania” would become the name used by US federal departments and agencies. But Canada has its own geographical naming authorities, so a US decision would not automatically change the lake’s official name in Canada.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Catastrophic failure: Bangladesh tank blast puts Chinese military hardware under spotlight
articles.summary: International News: A Chinese-origin Type 59 tank exploded during a live-fire exercise in Hathazari, Chattogram, killing two Bangladesh Army soldiers and seriously injuri.
articles.body: A Chinese-origin Type 59 tank exploded during a live-fire exercise in Hathazari, Chattogram, killing two Bangladesh Army soldiers and seriously injuring another, who was airlifted to the Combined Military Hospital in Dhaka. The Type 59 is China's domestically produced derivative of the Soviet T-54 main battle tank and has remained part of Bangladesh's armoured inventory for decades. Rather than retiring the ageing platforms, Bangladesh has continued upgrading them, with the Directorate General of Defence Procurement having previously issued documentation covering the upgrade of 40 T-59 tanks alongside the modernisation of 58 T-69IIG tanks.Even so, several buyers have shown clear signs of what can only be described as buyer's remorse. Thailand too had issues with its brand new and modern VT-4 tanks last year during a conflict with Cambodia, when tanks had their barrels blown while firing. With Pakistan, Venezuela and Iran having fielded Chinese air defence systems tat have failed to live up to advertised capabilities. Jordan put its six CH-4B armed drones up for resale within a year of acquiring them. In Iraq, eight of twenty CH-4B drones have crashed, while three Algerian drones of the same type went down in as many months, prompting several prospective buyers to look toward Türkiye instead.The incident lands at an awkward moment for Beijing's defence export ambitions. China remains the world's fifth-largest arms supplier, accounting for 5.6% of total global arms exports between 2021-25, according to SIPRI, with export volumes actually rising 11% compared to the previous five-year period. Roughly 77% of Chinese arms exports went to Asia and Oceania in this window, followed by Africa at 13%, with just one country, Pakistan, absorbing 61% of the total.After-sales support and quality of equipment provided remain a persistent complaint, according to MERICS a Berlin based think-tank. Bangladesh has reported issues with its K-8 jet trainers, F-7 fighters and FM-90 air defence missiles, while its army has faced problems with Chinese MBT-2000 tanks.Despite this, Bangladesh is now moving closer to becoming the third export customer for China's J-10CE fighter, after Pakistan and Uzbekistan, with a government panel preparing a draft agreement for formal negotiations. Local reports suggest Dhaka is eyeing up to 24 jets, with the aircraft alone estimated at around $1.2 billion, and the full package, including weapons, spares and training, closer to $2.2 billion, payments likely spread out until 2035-36 under the Forces Goal 2030 modernisation plan aimed at replacing Bangladesh's ageing F-7s and MiG-29s.

articles.title: In 1914, Tom Yawkey’s uncle bought Cat Island and nearby coastal land in Georgetown County; decades later, the 24,000-acre preserve sheltered woodpeckers and wetland birds
articles.summary: US News: Explore the remarkable story of the Tom Yawkey Wildlife Centre in South Carolina, from its origins in 1914 to its present-day role in wildlife conservation and research. Discover how this 24,000-acre preserve protects various habitats and species, supporting ecological and cultural history.
articles.body: In 1914, businessman William Yawkey’s uncle bought coastal land in South Carolina, setting in motion a conservation story that would unfold over more than a century. What began as a small holding along the shoreline of Georgetown County eventually became the Tom Yawkey Wildlife Centre, a 24,000-acre protected landscape where marshes, wetlands, pine forests, beaches and maritime forests now provide habitat for a remarkable range of wildlife.According to the South Carolina Department of Natural Resources, Tom Yawkey inherited the coastal property in 1925, after his uncle had purchased land there in 1914, and began investing in its conservation and preservation. In 1926, he purchased the remaining tracts of land from the South Island Hunting Club and began improving the property with wildlife protection in mind. The property eventually became the 24,000-acre Tom Yawkey Wildlife Center, which includes North Island, South Island, Sand Island and most of Cat Island at the mouth of Winyah Bay. Covering about 31 square miles, the preserve contains marshes, managed wetlands, upland pine forests, beaches and maritime forests, and is managed as a wildlife preserve, research area and waterfowl refuge.From private hunting land to a conservation legacyTom Yawkey is better known to many Americans as the longtime owner of the Boston Red Sox. But away from baseball, he developed a deep interest in wildlife and land management. According to the Tom Yawkey Wildlife Center, Yawkey was a self-taught ornithologist who spent years studying land-management techniques before bringing professional wildlife biologists into the effort. His aim was not simply to leave the property untouched, but to manage its varied habitats for waterfowl and other wildlife. The preserve includes freshwater and brackish wetlands, pine forests, maritime habitats, beaches and rice fields, creating a mix of ecosystems that support coastal wildlife. Currently, the research program at the centre includes studies of birds, alligators, sea turtles, flora, wetlands, and other parts of the coastal environment, which has encouraged more than 150 scientific papers to be published by the staff of this centre.According to a study published in The Anatomical Record, researchers examined a wild adult alligator that had been captured and measured five times over seven years at the Yawkey Wildlife Centre. The animal showed no discernible growth during that period, suggesting it had already reached skeletal maturity. Examination of its limb bones provided further evidence that growth had ceased. The study built on a much longer record of alligator research at the centre. Mark-recapture work there has been under way since 1979, allowing scientists to follow individual animals over periods of several decades. That long-term record makes the Yawkey property especially valuable for studying how animals live, grow and reproduce over time.A refuge for birds, wetlands and threatened wildlifeThe birds are among the creatures that benefit from this protected landscape. The landscape features several habitats which provide the birds with opportunities for both food and nesting. In 2022, according to the South Carolina Department of Natural Resources (SCDNR), the Yawkey Foundation donated another 269 acres on Cat Island to the department. The addition included 161 acres of upland pine forest habitat for the federally endangered red-cockaded woodpecker and 108 acres of managed wetland habitat for waterfowl, wading birds and shorebirds. The donation also helped preserve an important historic landmark, the Belle Isle Rice Mill Chimney, which is listed on the National Register of Historic Places. Standing 34 feet high, the chimney and its surrounding landscape offer a reminder of the rice culture that once shaped the South Carolina Lowcountry.This blend of natural and cultural history defines the centre. The islands it protects are far from untouched wilderness; they bear evidence of Indigenous and Gullah Geechee communities, historic agriculture, coastal habitation and changing patterns of land use. Archaeological and shoreline studies are currently being conducted to document and protect culturally significant sites threatened by sea-level rise and erosion. The centre also provides habitat for loggerhead sea turtles, while its wetlands support alligators and a wide range of other coastal wildlife. Alligator nesting research, for instance, continues at the site, highlighting the centre’s role in both conservation and scientific study.Why a century-old decision still mattersIn 2026, the Tom Yawkey Wildlife Center traces its conservation history back a century to 1926, when Tom Yawkey expanded the coastal property he had inherited and began acquiring additional land with wildlife protection in mind. The property remained under his stewardship for decades before he left it to the State of South Carolina in 1976. It was dedicated as a Heritage Preserve the following year, establishing the foundation for its continued protection as a public conservation area. Today, the 24,000-acre centre protects more than 7,000 acres of longleaf pine habitat that supports the federally endangered red-cockaded woodpecker, as well as wetlands important to waterfowl and other birds and beaches used by nesting loggerhead sea turtles. The landscape has therefore retained the conservation purpose that Yawkey began developing in the 1920s, while becoming part of South Carolina's long-term effort to protect its coastal wildlife.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Around 1,700 passengers boarded a Royal Caribbean Alaska cruise and waited on the ship in Vancouver; two days later, the entire sailing was canceled
articles.summary: US News: Around 1,700 passengers who had boarded Royal Caribbean’s Serenade of the Seas in Vancouver for an Alaska cruise were left without a voyage after the .
articles.body: Around 1,700 passengers who had boarded Royal Caribbean’s Serenade of the Seas in Vancouver for an Alaska cruise were left without a voyage after the entire sailing was cancelled because of ongoing maintenance work. The passengers had already spent time on the ship when they were told that the cruise would not go ahead.The seven-night Alaska cruise was originally scheduled to leave Vancouver on August 30, People's magazine reported. About a week before the planned departure, passengers were informed that the cruise would instead be shortened to five nights. The departure was also moved to September 1.Passengers were still invited to board the ship on September 1 and use it as a hotel while they waited for the vessel to leave Vancouver. About 1,700 passengers boarded, expecting the delayed cruise to eventually begin. However, the departure time passed without the ship leaving the port.Passengers were told that the departure had been delayed, but an announcement later informed them that Royal Caribbean had cancelled the entire sailing. Guests were given until midnight the following day to leave the ship, turning what had been planned as the beginning of an Alaska holiday into an unexpected scramble to make new travel arrangements.Why the cruise was cancelledRoyal Caribbean said the cancellation was linked to ongoing maintenance work on Serenade of the Seas. The cruise line did not provide details about the specific technical issue involved.“To accommodate ongoing maintenance, we’ve had to cancel our sailing,” a Royal Caribbean spokesperson told USA Today and Fox News. “We apologize to our guests for the inconvenience and have worked with them to adjust their travel plans.”The company had first told passengers about the maintenance issue before the original August 30 departure date. At that stage, the seven-night cruise was changed to a five-night sailing, while the departure was pushed back to September 1.Passengers were allowed to spend time on the ship while it remained in Vancouver. They could use much of the vessel and could also leave to explore the city. Some areas, including the casino, remained closed.Passengers scramble to change their plansArielle Anderson, a 28-year-old mother and lawyer from South Carolina, had booked the cruise as a gift for her family. She told USA Today that they had “been looking forward to this since Christmas.”The family had wanted to visit Alaska and had already travelled for the planned holiday. After the cruise was initially shortened, Anderson said cancelling the trip and getting refunds for their tickets would have been difficult because members of the family were flying in from different parts of the country.Instead, the family travelled to Whistler before boarding the ship on September 1.Anderson said passengers were instructed to board the vessel as part of the immigration process. Once on board, they waited for the ship to depart, but the expected departure time passed. Later, they were told that the departure had been delayed.By the evening, passengers were informed that the entire cruise had been cancelled. Anderson described the reaction among guests as chaotic.“Everybody was kind of panicking, so we were all just sitting in one of the bar areas, and everybody was just on their phones,” Anderson said. “People were really upset because everybody was trying to find flights and hotels and stuff.”Refunds and future cruise credit offeredRoyal Caribbean offered passengers affected by the cancellation a full refund. According to USA Today, the company also offered a 100% future cruise credit for the fare and reimbursement for flight change fees.Passengers were also set to receive a pro-rated refund for dining and beverage packages, according to the New York Post.For Anderson’s family, the cancelled cruise meant changing the holiday rather than ending it completely. Her mother found a rental car, and the family travelled to a vacation rental near Bellingham, Washington, while keeping their original flight home from Vancouver.“We just got an Airbnb down here, and have just been hanging out around here, hiking and whatnot,” Anderson said. “Definitely not what we planned, but [we’re] trying to make the best of it.”The cancellation also left other passengers wondering what would happen to later sailings involving the ship. Some raised questions on cruise message boards about future trips that had already been booked.According to CruiseMapper, Serenade of the Seas later departed Vancouver for another Alaska cruise on September 6.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Miami flight overrun: Plane touched down at nearly 300 kmph despite high-speed warning
articles.summary: US News: The US National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) has released preliminary findings into the runway overrun involving a 21 Air Boeing 767 at Miami In.
articles.body: The US National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) has released preliminary findings into the runway overrun involving a 21 Air Boeing 767 at Miami International Airport. It revealed that the cargo plane touched down at nearly 300 kmph, despite a pilot warning that it was travelling too fast. The investigation also found that the crew attempted a go-around after touchdown, while there was no indication that the aircraft's speed brakes or thrust reversers were deployed.The findings come from the cockpit voice recorder (CVR) and flight data recorder (FDR) recovered from 21 Air Flight 7598. The Boeing 767-33A was flying from San Juan, Puerto Rico, to Miami when it overran the end of Runway 30 after landing.What happened during the landing?The flight data shows that the aircraft was still travelling at 158 knots, or about 293 kmph, when its nose and right main landing gear touched down.The brakes were applied shortly afterwards, when the aircraft was travelling at 146 knots, or about 270 kmph. The left main landing gear touched down when the speed had dropped to 134 knots, or about 248 kmph.This means the aircraft was already on the runway at a relatively high speed, leaving the crew with less distance to slow down before reaching the end.The NTSB's data shows that the brakes were then released when the aircraft was travelling at 120 knots.At that point, the engines were briefly powered up in a manner consistent with an attempt to go around.The report says the throttles were then brought back to idle and the brakes were applied again. The aircraft was travelling at 117 knots at that stage.Pilots had noticed aircraft's speedThe cockpit recording suggests that speed had been a concern even before the aircraft touched down.During the approach, one pilot called for the flaps to be set to 20 degrees. The other pilot responded that they were travelling too fast.The pilot continued making comments about the aircraft's excessive speed during the remainder of the recording. The NTSB said there was no consistent verbal response to those comments.The report records the sequence as follows:"A pilot called for ﬂaps to be set to 20 degrees, and the other pilot cautioned they were too fast. The other pilot made additional comments regarding the aircr​aft’s excessive speed throughout the remainder of the recording. There was not a consistent verbal response to the comments about speed."The autopilot then appears to have been disconnected about 1 minute and 23 seconds before the end of the CVR recording.Aircraft issued multiple warningsThe aircraft also received several automated warnings as it approached the runway.The system issued a "sink rate sink rate" warning, followed by a "too low terrain" warning. The latter warning was repeated four times during the approach.The NTSB's preliminary timeline records:"Electronic “sink rate sink rate” callout."It later records:"Electronic “too low terrain” callout. Annunciated four times."Another "too low terrain" warning was recorded later during the approach.These warnings indicate that the aircraft's approach was generating alerts from its onboard warning systems as it descended towards the runway.Go-around was called, but aircraft had already landedThe cockpit recording shows that a pilot called for a go-around about 15 seconds after sounds consistent with the aircraft touching down.The FDR data also shows that the throttles were briefly increased to a setting consistent with go-around thrust.However, the engines were then brought back to idle and the brakes were applied again.The NTSB's data shows that there was no indication of the aircraft using its speed brakes or thrust reversers.In simple terms, the aircraft had landed, the crew attempted to initiate a go-around, but the aircraft then returned to idle engine power and braking was reapplied as it continued along the runway.The aircraft's recorded speed fell to 96 knots before the flight data recorder showed marked changes in its lateral, longitudinal and vertical acceleration.The final recorded groundspeed was 65 knots.What the recorders tell investigatorsThe NTSB recovered both recorders from the accident site and successfully read them at its Vehicle Recorder Laboratory in Washington DC.The cockpit voice recorder contained more than two hours of good-quality audio across four channels. The flight data recorder contained about 54 hours of information and recorded more than 400 parameters.Investigators will now conduct a more detailed review of the cockpit recording and prepare a written transcript.The NTSB stressed that the findings released on September 9 are preliminary and could change as the investigation continues.The current data, however, provides a clearer picture of the final moments: the aircraft approached and landed at high speed, the crew had raised concerns about speed, multiple automated warnings were heard, a go-around was called after touchdown, and there was no recorded indication that speed brakes or thrust reversers were deployed.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Kansas student lost his class ring during a snowball fight with his future wife: 53 years later, when campus workers dug it out, the couple happened to be passing through the city
articles.summary: US News: Kansas student lost his class ring during a snowball fight with his future wife: 53 years later, when campus workers dug it out, the couple happened t.
articles.body: Kansas student lost his class ring during a snowball fight with his future wife: 53 years later, when campus workers dug it out, the couple happened to be passing through the cityWhat are the odds of finding something lost for 53 years? Very slim. Now imagine it being discovered when its owner was driving through the same city, with the same person involved in the half-century-old incident, on the same stretch of highway. At some point, the coincidences start to feel almost impossible. And yet, that’s exactly what happened.Jim Burkhart lost his class ring to a snowball fight in 1973, while he was a student at Dodge City Community College (DC3). He wasn’t alone when he lost it. Marilyn Crockett was there, the woman he'd throw a snowball at with his left hand, the hand the ring sat on. She was there when it vanished into the Kansas dirt. Fifty-three years later, when the phone call came, she was there again, sitting next to him in the car, this time as his wife. The irrigation workers unearthed the ring while they were repairing the ground.This lost-and-found story gets so much better that, if you tried to pitch it as fiction, a filmmaker might send it back with a note: ‘Too many coincidences. The audience won’t buy it.’The ring lost in the 1970sJim Burkhart, a football player at DC3 in the early 1970s, lost the ring somewhere during the autumn of 1973. He was outside with Marilyn Crockett, the woman who would become his wife, and they were fooling around in the snow. Burkhart threw a snowball at her using his left hand, the same hand he wore his ring on. “I was feeling a little ornery… and I threw a snowball at her with my left hand,” Burkhart said, according to a news release by the college. He wore the ring on his left hand because of a childhood injury on his right. “She doesn’t remember if I hit her. I probably did. I had pretty good aim.”Whether or not the snowball reached the target, the ring surely flew off with the snowball. They searched the surrounding area. “We went back, looked a couple of times, and never did find the ring. And we would always kid about it. But yeah, we lost it that day,” he recalled. After the search turned up nothing, the couple moved on with their lives.Campus workers unearth the ringYears passed by: more than half a century, to be precise. Burkhart went on with his life, and the ring remained submerged in layers of dirt. On August 7, Daemian Serna and Craig Mellecker, members of the DC3 grounds crew, were finishing up excavation work near the Administration Building when Serna spotted something shining in the soil. “I thought it was a gold hose clamp, which we don’t have. So, my interest was pretty piqued,” Serna said. But once he brushed the soil off, he realised it was a ring. “It said Kinsley High School. It had a little coyote on it and 1973. Then, I cleaned it a little more, and I saw two initials, one on each side, J and B. Craig right away looks over, and he goes, ‘Oh, somebody’s going to want that.’”After finishing their work, they called Kinsley High School. “Within an hour, he had a name and a story, and he got in contact with Jim right away,” Serna said. The find was quite rare for the workers, too. During their work, they stumble upon lots of things, but not something like this. “Usually, I just find old soda cans or trash in the dirt. Not an old high school ring from 50 years ago!”The heartfelt reunionBurkhart and his wife, Marilyn Crockett, were driving to Tulsa that same day they got the call. In fact, they'd just visited Dodge City a week earlier, and during that visit, they'd talked once again about the missing ring. “You know, the ironic thing about the whole thing is, over the years, how many times we were in Dodge, and Marilyn would always bring up how we needed to go by the school and see if the ring was in the lost and found,” he said.Somewhere on the road, Burkhart's phone rang, with a woman on the other end asking if he'd lost a class ring on the college campus back in 1973. “I said, ‘Yeah, in 1973. I sure did.’ She said, ‘Well, they found it!’”For Serna, too, the whole incident was ‘kind of surreal’. “When we took him down to the quad, he went exactly where he remembered, and it was practically right there where we found it,” Serna said. “It’s really cool. It’s really movie-esque. It’s something you hear about in movies or on the news, not something you actually run into in real life!”About the coupleBurkhart and Marilyn hadn't initially dated as high school classmates. They'd started seeing each other the summer after graduation, just before enrolling at DC3 together. He studied general studies and played football. She worked towards a secretarial certificate. After his football career ended, Burkhart transferred to Emporia State and had a career in education. The couple got married in 1976 while he was still a student. He worked in Kansas for 37 years, in different roles including teacher, coach, and administrator. His work took them to Meriden, Deerfield, Mulvane, and, ultimately, Goddard. Marilyn worked in secretarial positions at many of the same schools. They raised two daughters and eventually settled in Goddard. They have four grandchildren now.Over the years, the lost ring became a favourite story retold during Thanksgiving and family dinners. And just like that, life came full circle for Burkhart and his wife when the ring was found. Marilyn said she planned to take the ring to a jewellery store to have it cleaned up properly—a ring that had survived in the Kansas soil through seasons and years that neither of them would have predicted when that snowball went flying through the air. “I’m going to take it to them and say, ‘You’re not going to believe this!’” she said.Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
